newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BLEWETT AND WAUGH PUT AUSTRALIA IN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BLEWETT AND WAUGH PUT AUSTRALIA IN CHARGE.

text.p: Greg Blewett's third test century and an unbroken 204-run fifth wicket partnership with Steve Waugh put Australia firmly in charge on the third day of the first test against South Africa at the Wanderers on Sunday.
At tea the visitors had reached 378 for four and extended their lead to 76 after bowling South Africa out for 302 on the first day.

Blewett on drove Allan Donald for his 17th four 10 minutes before tea to bring up his hundred from 223 deliveries and register the double century partnership at the same time. Blewett was 103 not out at the interval with Waugh on 93.

The batting from both men was characterised by the remorseless, ruthless orthodoxy of both attack and defence and the home team's six man bowling attack began wilting noticeably midway through the afternoon.

When the stand reached 158 it broke the previous highest fifth wicket record in 18 tests at the Wanderers. The old mark of 157 was set by South Africa's Tony Pithey and Johnny Waite in the 1964 series against England.

Donald bore the brunt of the Australian batting which became increasingly attack-orientated as tea approached and became the first to concede over 100 runs when Blewett registered his century. At tea Donald had conceded 113 runs from 29 overs while spnner Paul Adams had cost 92 from 34.
Waugh seemed happy to allow Blewett to take centre stage but there has been an air of inevitability about his imminent 12th test century from very early in his innings.
